::: {#sol-rate-sweep}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
rates = [0.003, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3]
sweep = pd.DataFrame(
    [
        {"width": width, "lr": lr, "seed": seed, "accuracy": train_and_score(width, lr, seed)[-1]}
        for width in [8, 512]
        for lr in rates
        for seed in range(3)
    ]
)
mean_accuracy = sweep.groupby(["width", "lr"])["accuracy"].mean().unstack("width")
best_rate = mean_accuracy.idxmax()
best_accuracy = mean_accuracy.max()
best_rate_8, best_rate_512 = best_rate[8], best_rate[512]
edge_accuracy_512 = mean_accuracy.loc[3, 512]
gap_at_01 = mean_accuracy.loc[0.1, 512] - mean_accuracy.loc[0.1, 8]
gap_at_best = best_accuracy[512] - best_accuracy[8]
print(mean_accuracy.round(3))
print(best_rate.to_dict(), gap_at_01, gap_at_best)
# Stop the render if the prose below stops being true.
assert best_rate[8] < best_rate[512] < max(rates)
assert 0 < gap_at_best < gap_at_01
```

::: {#fig-rate-sweep}

```{python}
#| fig-alt: "Validation accuracy against learning rate on a logarithmic axis from 0.003 to 3, for widths 8 and 512, with one dot per run and a line through the means of three seeds. Both curves rise with the learning rate and then fall to about 0.1 at learning rate 3. The width-512 curve rises earlier and peaks at learning rate 1, near 0.95; the width-8 curve peaks at 0.3, near 0.88."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5))
for width, marker in [(8, "o"), (512, "s")]:
    runs = sweep[sweep["width"] == width]
    ax.scatter(runs["lr"], runs["accuracy"], marker=marker, alpha=0.5, label=f"width {width}");
    ax.plot(mean_accuracy.index, mean_accuracy[width]);
ax.set_xscale("log");
ax.set_xlabel("learning rate");
ax.set_ylabel("validation accuracy");
ax.legend();
fig.tight_layout();
plt.show()
```

Final validation [accuracy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/metrics.html#def-accuracy) of each run in the sweep, and the mean over the three seeds at each [learning rate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-learning-rate).

:::

[Width](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/neural-nets.html#def-width) 8 does best with [learning rate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-learning-rate) `r py$best_rate_8`,
and width 512 with `r py$best_rate_512`.
At learning rate 0.1,
width 512's mean [accuracy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/metrics.html#def-accuracy) is higher by `r sprintf("%.3f", py$gap_at_01)`.
With each width at its own best rate,
it is higher by `r sprintf("%.3f", py$gap_at_best)`.
The wider network does classify better,
by about a third as much as the comparison at one rate said.

:::
